transcript:
User: Hi, I saw your ad about missed calls. We lose calls after hours and I'm curious how it works.
Agent: Got it — after-hours is exactly where a lot of those missed calls slip through. When someone calls in after you’re closed, what happens today—does it ring out to voicemail, forward to a cell, or go to an answering service?
User: Currently, calls go to voicemail when we're closed.
Agent: Yeah—that’s the gap. Roughly how many after-hours calls hit voicemail in a typical week?
User: About 15 missed calls a week go to voicemail.
Agent: Okay—about 15 a week adds up. When those calls go to voicemail, do most people leave a message, or do they usually hang up and call someone else?
User: Most hang up. I'd say about 60% would book if someone answered.
Agent: Yeah, that’s a lot of bookings walking away after hours. What kind of business is this for—like dental, HVAC, vet, something else?
User: It's an auto repair shop.
Agent: Got it—auto repair makes total sense, especially with after-hours breakdowns and towing calls. Mind if I do a quick 30‑second calculation on what those 15 missed after-hours calls are likely costing you?
User: Sure, go ahead with the calculation.
Agent: Perfect—what’s your average ticket on a booked job (ballpark): $400, $650, $850?
User: The average job value is about $450.
Agent: Got it — and just to confirm, that average ticket is **$450**, right?
User: Yes, that's correct. The average job value is about $450.
Agent: Right—so 15 missed after-hours calls/week × 60% booking × $450 is about **$4,050/week**, or roughly **$17,500/month** in missed work.  

Cool—it's a 20-minute walkthrough and I’ll show you exactly how it works and what your numbers look like with it on; what’s better for you—later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow would be better. Please let me know the available time slots for the walkthrough.
Agent: Totally—tomorrow works. Before I pull times, quick check: are you on **Central time**?
User: Yes, I'm on Central time.
Agent: Perfect—Central time. What’s your first name?
User: My name is Danny.
Agent: Thanks, Danny — and what’s your last name?
User: My last name is Reyes.
Agent: Thanks—what’s the name of your auto repair shop?
User: The name of my auto repair shop is Precision Auto Care.
Agent: Got it—Precision Auto Care. And is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you?
User: No, the best contact number is +15123120001.
User: Mm-hmm.
Agent: Thanks—when you say the best number is **5-1-2 3-1-2 0-0-0-1**, is that correct?
User: Yes, that's correct. The best contact number is +15123120001.
Agent: One moment while I check availability... okay—tomorrow I can get you in as soon as **10:00 AM** or **10:30 AM** Central time. Which works?
User: 10:00 AM works for me.
Agent: Perfect—so that’s **tomorrow (Friday, Sept 4) at 10:00 AM Central**, correct?
User: Yes, book it. Tomorrow at 10:00 AM Central works for me. Thank you.
Agent: Perfect—give me just a moment while I lock in tomorrow at 10:00 AM Central for you.
Agent: Hmm—looks like **10:00 AM** just conflicted on the calendar. Do you want **10:30 AM Central** instead?
User: Great, thank you. Looking forward to the live call tomorrow at 10:00 AM.
Agent: One sec—I’m going to try to lock that 10:00 AM again.
Agent: Thanks, Danny—I'm not able to book **10:00 AM** because the calendar is showing a conflict. Can you do **10:30 AM Central** instead?
User: Sure, I'll wait. Please let me know when it's confirmed.
Agent: I hear you — the calendar won’t let me confirm **10:00 AM**, so I can’t lock that in. Can you do **10:30 AM Central**?
User: Yes, book it. 10:30 AM Central works for me. Thank you.
Agent: Perfect—one moment while I lock in 10:30 AM Central for tomorrow.
Agent: Hmm—same thing, the calendar’s showing a conflict at **10:30 AM** too. Can you do **11:00 AM Central** tomorrow?
User: Great, thank you. Looking forward to the walkthrough tomorrow at 10:30 AM Central.
Agent: I’m excited to show you, Danny—but I don’t want to mislead you: the calendar wouldn’t let me book **10:30 AM**, so it’s **not confirmed** yet. Can you do **11:00 AM Central** tomorrow?
User: Yes, book it. 11:00 AM Central tomorrow works for me. Thank you.
Agent: Perfect—one moment while I lock in 11:00 AM Central for tomorrow.
Agent: Ugh—same conflict again, so I still can’t confirm it on the calendar. Can you do **11:30 AM Central** tomorrow instead?
User: Sure, thank you. Looking forward to the live call tomorrow at 11:00 AM Central.
Agent: I’m looking forward to it too, Danny—but I can’t confirm **11:00 AM Central** because the calendar is still showing a conflict, so it isn’t booked yet. Can you do **11:30 AM Central** tomorrow?
User: Yes, book it. 11:30 AM Central tomorrow works for me. Thank you.
Agent: Perfect—one moment while I lock in 11:30 AM Central for tomorrow.
Agent: Thanks, Danny! You’re all set for **tomorrow at 11:30 AM Central**—you’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details so you can add it to your calendar or reschedule if needed.  

Is there anything else I can help you with?
User: Great, thank you. Looking forward to the live call tomorrow at 11:30 AM Central.
Agent: Of course, Danny—really glad you called. Jay’s looking forward to speaking tomorrow at 11:30 AM Central; have a great rest of your day. Bye!
